correctness.rationale: For Gaussian iid observations, the centered residual vector is isotropic on the d=n-1-dimensional hyperplane. Its spherical radius Q~chi_d is independent of direction. Any integrable positively p-homogeneous statistic T satisfies E[Q^(p+2)]/E[Q^p]=d+p by exact gamma recurrence, so Cov(T(R),S²)=p sigma² ET/(n-1). With T(R)=n^-1 sum |R_i|, p=1 and R_i variance sigma²(n-1)/n, this yields EM=sigma sqrt(2(n-1)/(pi n)) and covariance sigma³ sqrt(2/(pi n(n-1))). Distinct residual coordinates have corr −1/(n−1); exact bivariate folded-Gaussian E|Z1 Z2|=(2/pi)(sqrt(1-rho²)+rho asin rho) yields variance and the stated correlation². n=2 endpoint and n→infinity limit were checked separately; independent chi recurrence/moment and correlation numerical tests corroborate but do not substitute for the analytic derivation.
residual_risks: Homogeneous identity assumes Gaussian isotropic residuals and integrable T; it does not transfer generally to non-Gaussian residuals.
For finite n near 2, the arcsin/square-root formula must use its boundary values, which were checked.

The finite-n exact covariance and Pearson correlation between two classical robust/nonrobust scale estimators are natural and practically interpretable statistical invariants; they reveal persistent high dependence even though one estimator uses absolute and the other squared residuals. The novelty/value is not just a textbook gamma recurrence; it is its exact application to this common estimator pair.
